title: Cohort observability: metric definitions + trace playbook
content:
Purpose
This is a lightweight working doc to align on cohort-based observability for tokenized inference workloads. The goal is to make cohort-level regressions obvious in dashboards and traces so product and infra teams can: 1) detect degradations that only hit specific customer segments, 2) attribute cost/latency differences to model/config choices (quantization, batching policies, model family), and 3) provide clear rollbacks/fallback criteria in rollouts.

Scope and motivation
- Problem: global SLOs and single-tenant aggregates hide regressions that only affect a subset (trial users, high-concurrency tenants, long-context sessions).
- Why cohorts: product tiers, onboarding vs production traffic, nightly-batch jobs, synthetic traffic, and edge-case prompt types often have systematically different distributions (seq len, reuse of prefixes) that change latency/cost and KV cache behavior.
- Outcome: dashboards + traces that let an engineer go from alert -> cohort breakdown -> representative trace -> remediation in under 15 minutes.

High-level approach
1) Define cohort labels and tagging hygiene (required ingestion tags).
2) Define a small set of cohort-focused SLIs and derived metrics (p50/p95/p99 where needed).
3) Implement sampling/tracing anchors that preserve cohort context across async hops and fallbacks.
4) Build a dashboard template that surfaces the right comparisons and cost attribution, plus a small playbook for investigation steps.

Cohort taxonomy (recommended canonical labels)
- cohort: "trial", "paid-starter", "paid-pro", "enterprise", "internal", "synthetic"
- workload_shape: "short-chat", "long-context", "streaming", "embedding-batch"
- route_type: "chat", "completion", "embed", "rerank"
- rollout_bucket: "canary-1", "canary-2", "stable"
Notes: cohort must be set at the API gateway layer so it is present in request logs, traces, and metric labels. If unknown, set "cohort=unknown" not empty.

Required metric definitions (names + short definition)
- requests.count: counter of inference requests (label: cohort, model_family, route_type).
- tokens.generated.count: total tokens emitted (tokenization must be consistent across model families).
- latency.request_p50_ms / request_p95_ms / request_p99_ms: end-to-end request latency from gateway receive -> final token emission end. Tags include cohort, model_family, quantization_profile, region.
- batching.delay_p95_ms: time a request waits in serving queue before being batched (measured between enqueue -> batch dispatch). Important to capture per-cohort because small tenants may get different batching behavior.
- kv.prefix_cache_hit_rate: ratio of requests served from prefix/KV cache (tags: cohort, model_variant, cache_key_version). Use name kv.prefix_cache_hit_rate_by_cohort for dashboards.
- kv.kv_population_age_seconds: histogram of time since prefix was populated. Helps identify TTL/eviction hotspots for certain cohorts.
- failures.total.count + failures.type{timeout,oom,decode_error}: error taxonomy by cohort.
- cost.cpu_seconds_per_request & cost.gpu_seconds_per_request: derived metrics to attribute spend to cohorts (should be computed using request-level attribution exported from runtime).
- quality.hallucination_rate_by_eval: fraction of eval prompts failing quality thresholds (for post-deploy quality guardrails). Labeled by cohort when possible.

Tagging/label hygiene (must-have dimensions)
- tenant_id (or anonymous_tenant_hash) - required for billing/cohort-mapping but PII controls required
- cohort - as defined above
- model_family (e.g., rw-13b, rw-7b-quantized)
- model_variant (model version id)
- quantization_profile (none, int8, nf4)
- route_type (chat/completion/embed)
- rollout_bucket (canary/stable)
- region
- request_id and trace_id (for trace linking)

Trace design and sampling
- Trace anchors: put cohort, model_family, and rollout_bucket as attributes on the root span so any child span can be filtered. Root span should be created in the API gateway layer.
- Adaptive sampling: sample more aggressively for cohorts with high cost or for new canary buckets. Rules: sample 100% of traces for rollout_bucket =~ canary-* for the first 72h; sample 10% for enterprise tenants and 1% default for public free tier.
- Representative traces: define 3 candidate criteria to auto-flag a trace as "representative": p95 latency for cohort, low cache hit and high token count, or error span present. These flagged traces should surface in the dashboard and be persisted longer in trace storage.
- Span breadcrumbing: include markers for kv_cache.hit/miss, batch.wait, model.kv_load, and fallback.model_switch. Markers should be 1-line messages with standardized fields: {event, cohort, model_variant, cache_key}.

Dashboard layout (template sections)
A. Cohort overview row (select cohort from dropdown)
 - requests.count (timeseries)
 - request latency p50/p95/p99
 - tokens per request p50/p95
 - kv.prefix_cache_hit_rate (gauge + timeseries)
 - cost per 1K tokens (derived)
B. Dimension breakdowns (small multiples by model_family)
 - latency heatmap (seq_len bucket vs latency)
 - batching.delay distribution
 - prefix_cache hit rate vs kv_population_age
C. Regression lanes (compare cohort vs global and vs previous deploy)
 - percent delta widgets (latency, error rate, cost) with traffic-weighted significance
D. Representative traces panel
 - list of flagged traces (with direct link to trace viewer) + short metadata (latency, tokens, cache_hit)
E. Investigation links and playbook
 - common causes checklist (KV eviction, noisy long-context tenant, model_variant bad latency)
 - runbook links (INF-xxxx)

Investigation playbook (step-by-step)
1) Alert fired (e.g. cohort p95 latency increased >20% and traffic >1% of global).
2) Open cohort dashboard -> confirm metric and check related dimensions (model_family, region).
3) Inspect batching.delay_p95 and kv.prefix_cache_hit_rate_by_cohort. If batching delay spiked, check autoscaler/backpressure.
4) Open representative traces -> look for model.kv_load spans and fallback.model_switch. If fallback occurred, correlate to model_variant rollout.
5) If error spikes, check failures.type taxonomy and match to GitHub PRs or infra incidents.
6) If it's a rollout issue, tag rollout_bucket in alert, instruct product to pause canary and rollback per rollback playbook.

Implementation notes and gotchas
- Avoid high cardinality labels in time-series metrics. cohort and model_family are okay; tenant_id should be reserved for trace-level only (and used in aggregated billing exports), not time-series metrics.
- For kv metrics: do not use raw prompt text as cache_key label. Use hashed cache_key with stable version id to avoid leakage and cardinality explosion.
- Make sure synthetic cohort is flagged early so SREs can ignore expected weekends/load.
- Normalization: when comparing cohorts, normalize by tokens_generated to avoid misleading p50 comparisons when traffic shape is different.

Open questions / decisions needed
- How long do we keep cohort-level trace samples by default? (proposal: 90d for canary, 30d for enterprise, 14d for default)
- Do we allow tenant_id as a Prometheus label for billing exports? (privacy concerns; prefer daily aggregated CSVs instead).
- Should fallback.model_switch be surfaced as an alertable signal for canary buckets? (pro: early detection, con: noisy during controlled experiments)

Next steps (action items)
- [ ] INF-2148: Add cohort tag to API gateway (owner: Ethan)
- [ ] Telemetry PR: add kv.prefix_cache_hit_rate and kv_population_age histogram (owner: Zoe) -> PR linked above
- [ ] Dashboard: create cohort dashboard template (owner: Maya)
- [ ] Tracing: implement canary sampling policy + representative trace flagging (owner: Liam)

Notes to reviewers
- This is intentionally lightweight and pragmatic. Focus on: are the cohort labels useful? Are these the right handful of metrics to capture regressions? Does the dashboard layout make the investigation flow <15 minutes?
- If you have additional cohort types (e.g., partners, offline-batch), add to taxonomy above and flag expected traffic patterns.

Quick reference (cheat sheet)
- Key SLIs to watch per cohort: request_p95_latency, kv.prefix_cache_hit_rate, tokens_per_request_p95, failures.total.count, cost.gpu_seconds_per_1k_tokens.

-- end --
